title: Mother, prayer and the first trumpet lessons
summary: His mother prayed when she could not afford more lessons; his father earned extra money killing chickens and fixing clocks.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. We're on reel number two with Wallace Davenport in November the 14th, 1995. Tell me the story about your mother and the horn. How'd you get your first horn?

Well, at the school, McDonald's 36, the kids who wanted to play music, they had to put up a dollar a week. And most of the dollar was for the horn. And after 50 lessons, the horn is yours. So the horn didn't cost for $50. No, it didn't cost $50. It cost $20. It cost $25. So, and yeah, when she said she was going to turn the horn in because she couldn't pay for any more lessons. And I cried so much until she went and got on a knee and started praying. She was the type of woman that believed in her. She believed in prayers. And she prayed and asked the Lord to let her give me some more lessons, pay for some more lessons. And something happened. She got another little job. See, because the job she had, she wasn't making but a dollar a week. And my father, well, he was a jack of all trades. He used to do things for people in the neighborhood and they would pay him. Like, at the time, like when you go to a grocery store and buy chicken or turkey, they didn't have any frozen chicken and turkey. You had to buy them alive and take him home and kill him. Well, a lot of those men in the neighborhood, a lot of women, they didn't know how to kill a chicken. So they would get my dad and give him fifty cents to kill the chicken. And he would save that money up and that kind of helped to pay for our music lessons. And he did a lot of things making extra money. But the extra money he made wasn't much. He might fix your clock for ten cents, a nickel. There wasn't much money around then. And like when we'd go to church, we used to put a penny in the collection. And something old. When they passed the flag. Yeah, we put a penny. But at that time,
